newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Life unlikely to hurt financial system - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Life unlikely to hurt financial system - MOF.

text.p: Troubles at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co are unlikely to have any directly adverse effects on the overall Japanese financial system, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told a parliamentary committee meeting on Friday afternoon.

"We do not think that this (the Nissan Life incident) will have a direct negative impact on Japan's financial system," said Makoto Fukuda, director of the insurance department at the ministry's banking bureau.

He said that insurance firms do not have a settlement function like banks and do not have bank borrowings, nor does their business overlap with banks' business, so the failure of an insurance firm would not directly affect banks.
He added that Nissan Life's policies and assets would be transferred while its business is halted.
"So I do not think there will be any selling of securities that could cause confusion in the securities markets," he said.

The Finance Ministry said on Friday it had ordered Nissan Life to halt all operations except for servicing current customers, the first time the government has forced an insurer to shut down in the postwar period.

Fukuda said that since the Nissan Life incident would be handled through financial support functions within the industry, he could not think of any impact it might have on industries outside the insurance sector.
"The life insurance firm is a small-to-medium sized company which operates only in the domestic market. I cannot think of it having any international impact."
